title: Sentences with 是 (to be)
simpleExplanation: 是 (shì) links two nouns, like the verb «to be» in English: «A is B».
technicalExplanation: 是 is a copular verb that identifies or classifies the subject. Unlike English, it is never used to link a subject and an adjective: for that, 很 or another degree adverb is used.
usage: To identify people or things: professions, nationalities, identities.
avoidWhen: Never before a simple adjective: do not say 我是忙, but 我很忙.

negativeExamples.note: Incorrect: adjectives do not take 是. Say 我很忙.

commonMistakes: Using 是 with adjectives by influence of English «to be».

title: Adjectives with 很
simpleExplanation: Adjectives are linked to the subject with 很 (hěn), without a verb «to be».
technicalExplanation: In Chinese, adjectives function as predicates by themselves. 很 acts as a neutral link; without it, the sentence usually implies contrast. Its meaning of «very» is greatly weakened.
usage: To describe states and qualities: 我很好, 天气很热.
avoidWhen: Do not use it if there is already another degree adverb (真, 非常, 太).

negativeExamples.note: Incorrect: do not use 是 with adjectives.

commonMistakes: Always translating 很 as «very»: it is often just a link.

title: Questions with 吗
simpleExplanation: Add 吗 (ma) at the end of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question.
technicalExplanation: 吗 is an unstressed interrogative modal particle placed at the absolute final position. It does not alter the word order.
usage: Yes/no questions: 你是老师吗？
avoidWhen: It is not combined with interrogative pronouns (什么, 哪儿…) nor with the V不V form.

negativeExamples.note: Incorrect: 什么 already makes the sentence interrogative.

title: Possession with 的
simpleExplanation: 的 (de) marks possession or belonging: 我的书 = «my book».
technicalExplanation: 的 is a structural particle that subordinates the preceding element as a modifier of the following one. With close relationships (family, institutions) it is often omitted.
usage: Possessives and modifiers: 老师的名字, 中国的历史.
avoidWhen: It is omitted with family and close relationships: 我妈妈, 我们学校.

negativeExamples.note: Poor style: avoid chaining too many 的.

commonMistakes: Using 的 with family members where it sounds unnatural.

title: Negation with 不 and 没
simpleExplanation: 不 negates the present, future, and habits; 没 negates the past and possession.
technicalExplanation: 不 expresses volitional or habitual negation; 没(有) negates the realization of an event (perfective aspect) and is the only possible negation of 有.
usage: 不喝咖啡 (I don't drink coffee, habit); 没喝咖啡 (I haven't drunk coffee).
avoidWhen: Never 不有: possession is always negated with 没有.

negativeExamples.note: Incorrect: 有 is negated with 没.
Incorrect for completed past: use 没去.

commonMistakes: Using 不 to negate past actions.

title: Basic word order: Subject + Verb + Object
simpleExplanation: The neutral word order in Chinese is the same as English: subject, verb, object.
technicalExplanation: Chinese is an SVO language with a strong topic-comment tendency. Time and place complements go before the verb, not at the end as in English.
usage: 我学汉语。他喝茶。
avoidWhen: Do not put time at the end: 我明天去北京, not 我去北京明天.

examples.translation: I am going to Beijing tomorrow.
examples.translation_en: I am going to Beijing tomorrow.

negativeExamples.note: Incorrect: time goes before the verb.

commonMistakes: Placing time or place expressions at the end of the sentence.

title: Measure words: 个 and friends
simpleExplanation: A measure word always goes between a number and a noun: 一个人, 三本书.
technicalExplanation: Measure words (量词) categorize the noun. 个 is the generic one; 本 for books, 杯 for cups, 位 for people with respect. They also appear after demonstratives: 这个, 那本.
usage: Counting anything: 两个朋友, 五本书.
avoidWhen: Never omit the measure word: 三书 is incorrect.
